This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user resumed a previous session where 100+ autonomous Claude agents had been built for QuizSnap (a Shopify embedded app for product recommendation quizzes). The user sent a new message during this session requesting:
   - **Strict Shopify Polaris React UI/UX enforcement** across all agents — "make sure all agent and all follow strict shopify polaris react UI UX componenet library for any compoenenet to ensure its look fully shopiofy offical app type"
   - **Update all required agents** with Polaris patterns
   - **Create a production plan** for approval: "if there anything need to craft production grade app make plan i will approve it"
   - **Research top competitors** (Octane AI, Jebbit, RecoQuiz, Interact, Typeform) and ensure QuizSnap beats them: "research all top competitior functions and a-z thing and make sure in our implement betetr than those way"
   - **Build a Shopify-native official production-grade app** with "very structured and very stable backend"

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Shopify Polaris v13**: Strict enforcement of `tone` (not `status`) on Badge/Banner, `variant` (not boolean) on Button, `BlockStack`/`InlineStack` (not legacy `Stack`), `Card` without `sectioned` prop, `backAction` (not `breadcrumbs`), `Layout.AnnotatedSection` for settings
   - **App Bridge v4 Toast Pattern**: `shopify.toast.show()` via `useAppBridge()` hook — NEVER use `<Toast>` from `@shopify/polaris` or `<Frame>` wrapper in embedded apps
   - **React Router 7**: All imports from `react-router` not `@remix-run/react` (critical fix)
   - **App Bridge v4 Modals**: Use `<ui-modal>` web component for parent-frame modals; prefer inline Banner confirmations for destructive actions
   - **Canonical Schema Field Names**: `shop` (not `shopId`), `productGid` (not `shopifyProductId`), `status: "active" | "archived"` (not `isAvailable: Boolean`), `syncedAt` (not `lastSyncedAt`)
   - **Prisma v6**: Shop-scoped queries mandatory — `where: { shop: session.shop }`
   - **Auth Law**: `authenticate.admin(request)` first in every loader/action
   - **Zero Tailwind, Zero custom CSS, Zero `any` types** in admin UI
   - **Claude Agent System**: 101 `.claude/agents/*.md` files with YAML frontmatter, AUTO-DETECT triggers, DECISION TREE, SPAWN AGENTS, complete TypeScript code, SELF-VALIDATION CHECKLIST, NEVER rules
   - **Competitor Analysis**: Octane AI ($50-200/mo), Jebbit (enterprise), RecoQuiz ($19-79/mo), Interact ($27-99/mo), Typeform ($25-99/mo) — all beaten by QuizSnap's deeper Shopify integration, better pricing, AI quiz builder

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`.claude/agents/polaris-design-system.md`** (NEW — File #101)
     - Created as the definitive Polaris v13 bible that ALL other agents must reference
     - Contains: complete breaking changes table, every component reference (Page, Layout, Card, Forms, Navigation, Tables, Banners, Empty States, Skeletons, Modals, Metric Cards, Badges, Filters, Pagination), Polaris color tokens, spacing scale (025-1000), typography variants
     - Key pattern:
     ```tsx
     // App Bridge v4 toast — NOT Polaris Toast/Frame
     const shopify = useAppBridge();
     shopify.toast.show("Quiz saved!", { duration: 3000 });
     shopify.toast.show("Failed", { isError: true });
     // NEVER: <Frame><Toast content="..." /></Frame>
     ```

   - **`.claude/agents/ui-specialist.md`** (UPGRADED)
     - Complete quiz editor with 5-tab layout pattern
     - Full quiz list page with IndexFilters
     - Design tab with theme editor
     - Strict enforcement: "Never use `style={{ display: 'flex' }}` — use `<InlineStack>`"
     - Key quiz editor pattern:
     ```tsx
     <Page
       title={quiz.title}
       backAction={{ content: "Quizzes", url: "/app/quizzes" }}
       primaryAction={{ content: "Publish quiz", onAction: handlePublish, loading: isPublishing }}
       titleMetadata={<Badge tone={statusTone}>{quiz.status}</Badge>}
     >
       <Tabs tabs={QUIZ_EDITOR_TABS} selected={selectedTab} onSelect={setSelectedTab} fitted>
         <Card><BlockStack gap="400">...</BlockStack></Card>
       </Tabs>
     </Page>
     ```

   - **`.claude/agents/admin-builder.md`** (UPDATED)
     - Fixed Toast/Frame anti-pattern throughout
     - Changed `import { Toast, Frame }` to `import { useAppBridge } from "@shopify/app-bridge-react"`
     - Changed from `useState` toast management to `shopify.toast.show()`
     - Changed `<Frame><Page>` wrapper to plain `<Page>`
     - Updated NEVER rules and checklist to explicitly ban Toast/Frame pattern
     - Changed Settings page to use `Layout.AnnotatedSection` pattern

   - **`.claude/agents/question-builder.md`** (UPGRADED)
     - Added complete Polaris UI section for question editor
     - `AnswerRow` component with product tag management using Polaris `Tag` component
     - `SliderSettings`, `MultipleChoiceSettings`, `EmailCaptureSettings` with strict Polaris FormLayout
     - Key pattern:
     ```tsx
     <Box background="bg-surface-secondary" borderWidth="025" borderColor="border" borderRadius="200" padding="300">
       <BlockStack gap="200">
         <InlineStack gap="200" blockAlign="center">
           <Badge>{String(index + 1)}</Badge>
           <Box width="100%"><TextField label={`Option ${index + 1}`} labelHidden .../></Box>
         </InlineStack>
       </BlockStack>
     </Box>
     ```

   - **`.claude/agents/modal-manager.md`** (UPDATED)
     - Fixed `ConfirmModal` to use `<ui-modal>` web component (App Bridge v4)
     - Fixed `useFetcher` import from `react-router` (not `@remix-run/react`)
     - Fixed `destructive` prop on Button → `tone="critical"` (Polaris v13)
     - Added inline Banner confirmation pattern as preferred alternative
     - Updated NEVER rules to ban `window.confirm()` and `@remix-run/react` imports

   - **`.claude/agents/billing-manager.md`** (UPGRADED)
     - Added complete pricing page `app/routes/app.billing.tsx` implementation
     - 4-plan comparison grid using Polaris `Grid` component
     - Annual/monthly billing toggle with 20% discount
     - Current usage section
     - Key pattern:
     ```tsx
     <Grid>
       {Object.entries(PLANS).map(([planId, plan]) => (
         <Grid.Cell key={planId} columnSpan={{ xs: 6, sm: 6, md: 3, lg: 3 }}>
           <Card background={planId === "pro" ? "bg-surface-success" : undefined}>
             <BlockStack gap="400">
               <InlineStack align="space-between">
                 <Text variant="headingLg">{plan.name}</Text>
                 {isCurrent && <Badge tone="success">Current plan</Badge>}
               </InlineStack>
               <Text variant="heading2xl" fontWeight="bold">{getPrice(plan)}</Text>
               <Button variant="primary" fullWidth onClick={() => submit({ intent: "upgrade", planId })}>
                 Upgrade to {plan.name}
               </Button>
             </BlockStack>
           </Card>
         </Grid.Cell>
       ))}
     </Grid>
     ```

   - **`.claude/agents/product-sync.md`** (FIXED — Critical Schema Errors)
     - Fixed wrong field names throughout:
       - `shopId` → `shop`
       - `shopifyProductId` → `productGid`
       - `isAvailable: false` → `status: "archived"` (Law 15 soft-delete)
       - `lastSyncedAt` → `syncedAt`
       - Removed `variants` field (not in canonical schema)
     - Fixed unique constraint key: `shop_productGid` (not `shopId_shopifyProductId`)
     - Added complete `syncProducts()` function with correct field names
     - Added product webhook handler with correct soft-delete pattern
     - Added Admin Sync UI section using Polaris

   - **`.claude/agents/quiz-builder.md`** (UPDATED)
     - Replaced `<Modal>` + `<Toast>` pattern with inline Banner confirmation
     - Changed `primaryAction={{ content: "Delete", destructive: true }}` → `tone="critical"`
     - Replaced toast state management with `shopify.toast.show()` comment

   - **8 agents batch-fixed** for `@remix-run/react` → `react-router`:
     - `bug-fixer.md`, `bulk-operations-builder.md`, `feature-flag-builder.md`, `notification-center-builder.md`, `pagination-builder.md`, `real-time-builder.md`, `search-filter-builder.md`, `state-manager.md`

   - **8 agents batch-fixed** for Polaris Toast/Frame removal:
     - `bug-fixer.md`, `bulk-operations-builder.md`, `email-integration.md`, `quiz-builder.md`, `quiz-embed-code-generator.md`, `results-builder.md`, `reviewer.md`, `template-builder.md`

   - **`.claude/commands/feature.md`** (UPGRADED)
     - Complete agent routing table with correct agent names
     - 6-step implementation process with quality gate checklist
     - Fixed wrong agent references (`polaris-specialist` → `polaris-design-system`, `validation-specialist` → `form-validator`)
     - Explicit Polaris v13 enforcement rules in implementation steps

   - **`.claude/commands/fix.md`** (UPGRADED)
     - Diagnosis process with error type routing table
     - Critical schema field name correction reference table
     - Common Polaris v13 fixes reference table
     - Fix verification checklist

4. Errors and Fixes:
   - **`Write tool "File has not been read yet"` error**: Attempted to write `fix.md` without reading it first. Fixed by reading the file first with `limit: 5` then writing.
   - **Background agents failed with Write permission denied**: Three background agents (rewrite 16 agents, create 25 new agents batch 2, rewrite 20 commands) were denied Write tool permissions. Handled by performing the work directly in the main conversation instead.
   - **Wrong schema field names in product-sync.md**: Agent was using `shopId`, `shopifyProductId`, `isAvailable`, `lastSyncedAt` which don't match the canonical CLAUDE.md Section 4 schema. Fixed by editing product-sync.md with correct field names.
   - **`@remix-run/react` imports in 8 agents**: These should import from `react-router` in React Router 7. Fixed via batch sed command.
   - **Polaris Toast/Frame pattern in multiple agents**: Using deprecated `<Toast>` from `@shopify/polaris` with `<Frame>` wrapper. Fixed by removing these patterns and replacing with `shopify.toast.show()` comment/pattern.

5. Problem Solving:

   - **Schema Alignment**: Fixed `product-sync.md` to use exact canonical field names from CLAUDE.md Section 4, with a field mapping table showing wrong → correct names.
   - **Toast/Frame Pattern**: The key fix was establishing that in App Bridge v4 embedded Shopify apps, notifications must use `shopify.toast.show()` not the Polaris `<Toast>` + `<Frame>` pattern. This was applied across all affected agents.
   - **Command Upgrades**: The 20 command files needed fixing for wrong agent references (`polaris-specialist`, `validation-specialist` don't exist) and outdated patterns. Started upgrading with correct agent names and Polaris enforcement rules.

Review recent changes in QuizSnap: $ARGUMENTS

## Agent Orchestration

| Review Phase            | Agent                | Focus Area                          |
|-------------------------|----------------------|-------------------------------------|
| Automated checks        | lint-runner          | TypeScript, ESLint, Prisma          |
| Security audit          | security-auditor     | Auth, CSRF, data exposure, scoping  |
| Shopify compliance      | shopify-compliance   | API usage, billing, webhooks, GDPR  |
| Code quality            | code-reviewer        | Patterns, readability, conventions  |
| API contracts           | api-reviewer         | Request/response shapes, validation |

## Process

### Phase 1: Automated Checks
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and capture all errors
- Run `npx eslint . --ext .ts,.tsx` and capture warnings/errors
- Run `npx prisma validate` to check schema integrity
- Check for any TODO or FIXME comments in changed files

### Phase 2: Security Audit
- Verify every loader/action calls `authenticate.admin(request)` or `authenticate.public.appProxy(request)`
- Confirm all Prisma queries include `shopId` in WHERE clauses (shop scoping)
- Check that no secrets, API keys, or tokens are hardcoded
- Verify CORS headers on public API endpoints use allowlist, not wildcard
- Ensure user input is sanitized before database insertion
- Check for SQL injection risk in any raw queries
- Verify CSRF tokens on all mutation actions

### Phase 3: Shopify Compliance
- Confirm webhook handlers validate HMAC signatures
- Check that billing API usage follows Shopify patterns
- Verify GDPR endpoints exist (customer data request, erasure, shop erasure)
- Ensure app scopes match what the app actually uses
- Check that AppBridge integration is correct for embedded app context

### Phase 4: Code Quality
- Verify adherence to patterns defined in CLAUDE.md
- Check for proper error handling (try/catch, error boundaries)
- Review naming conventions (files, functions, variables, routes)
- Look for code duplication that should be extracted to shared utilities
- Verify Polaris components are used correctly (no custom CSS overrides)
- Check that loading states and empty states are handled
- Review TypeScript types (no unnecessary `any`, proper generics)

### Phase 5: API Contract Review
- Verify loader return types match what the UI expects
- Check action responses include proper status codes and error messages
- Confirm API endpoints document their request/response shape
- Verify pagination is implemented for list endpoints
- Check rate limiting considerations for public endpoints

## Output Format

```
## Code Review Report

### Summary
- **Files Reviewed**: [count]
- **Overall Assessment**: [SHIP / SHIP WITH FIXES / DO NOT SHIP]

### Critical Issues (must fix before shipping)
1. [Issue description] — [file:line]
   - **Risk**: [What could go wrong]
   - **Fix**: [Suggested fix]

### Quality Issues (should fix soon)
1. [Issue description] — [file:line]
   - **Suggestion**: [Recommended improvement]

### Security Findings
- Auth checks: [PASS/FAIL — details]
- Shop scoping: [PASS/FAIL — details]
- Input validation: [PASS/FAIL — details]
- CORS policy: [PASS/FAIL — details]

### Shopify Compliance
- Webhook HMAC: [PASS/FAIL]
- GDPR endpoints: [PASS/FAIL]
- Billing integration: [PASS/FAIL]
- App scopes: [PASS/FAIL]

### Recommendation
[Ship recommendation with any conditions]
```

- [ ] All public endpoints validate input
- [ ] Webhook handlers verify HMAC signatures

## Agent Orchestration

## Models Reference

| Model              | Key Fields                                                        | Constraints                     |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| Session            | id, shop, state, accessToken, scope                               | Managed by Shopify auth         |
| Shop               | id, shopifyDomain, name, email, plan, onboardingCompleted         | Unique on shopifyDomain         |
| Quiz               | id, shopId, title, slug, status, type, settings (JSON)            | FK to Shop, unique slug per shop|
| Question           | id, quizId, type, title, description, position, settings (JSON)   | FK to Quiz, ordered by position |
| QuestionOption     | id, questionId, label, value, imageUrl, position                  | FK to Question                  |
| LogicRule          | id, quizId, sourceQuestionId, condition, targetQuestionId, action | FK to Quiz and Questions        |
| ResultProfile      | id, quizId, title, description, imageUrl, productIds (JSON)       | FK to Quiz                      |
| ScoreMapping       | id, resultProfileId, questionOptionId, score                      | FK to ResultProfile, Option     |
| QuizResponse       | id, quizId, shopId, respondentEmail, completedAt, answers (JSON)  | FK to Quiz, Shop                |
| AnalyticsEvent     | id, quizId, shopId, eventType, metadata (JSON), createdAt         | FK to Quiz, Shop, indexed       |
| EmailIntegration   | id, shopId, provider, apiKey (encrypted), listId, settings (JSON) | FK to Shop                      |
| ABTest             | id, quizId, variantA, variantB, splitPercent, status              | FK to Quiz                      |
| BillingPlan        | id, shopId, planName, chargeId, status, activatedAt               | FK to Shop                      |

## Process: Schema Changes

1. Read current `prisma/schema.prisma` to understand existing models
2. Plan the change — add model, add field, modify field, add relation
3. Apply the change to schema.prisma
4. Run `npx prisma validate` to check syntax
5. Run `npx prisma db push` to apply to dev database
6. Run `npx prisma generate` to update the Prisma client
7. Update any TypeScript types that reference the changed models

## Process: Query Optimization

1. Identify the slow query (check loader/action files)
2. Analyze the query — look for N+1 problems, missing includes, large selects
3. Add proper `select` clauses to fetch only needed fields
4. Add `include` for required relations instead of separate queries
5. Add database indexes in schema.prisma if needed (`@@index`)
6. Use `findMany` with `take`/`skip` for pagination
7. Consider caching for frequently-read, rarely-changed data

## Process: Data Operations

1. Identify the operation scope (single shop, all shops, specific records)
2. ALWAYS include `shopId` in WHERE clauses — never operate across shops
3. Use Prisma transactions for multi-step operations
4. Validate input data before writing to the database
5. Handle unique constraint violations gracefully

## Caution Rules

- NEVER delete data without explicit confirmation — soft delete preferred
- NEVER run raw SQL unless Prisma cannot express the query
- ALWAYS back up before destructive schema changes in production
- ALWAYS scope queries by shopId to maintain data isolation
- NEVER store sensitive data (API keys, tokens) in plain text — use encryption
- NEVER modify the Session model — it is managed by Shopify's auth system
- ALWAYS use transactions when updating multiple related records

Build an API endpoint for QuizSnap: $ARGUMENTS

## Agent Orchestration

| API Type                  | Primary Agent       | Support Agents            |
|---------------------------|---------------------|---------------------------|
| Admin API (internal)      | api-builder         | validation-specialist     |
| Public storefront API     | storefront-builder  | api-builder, cors-manager |
| Webhook receiver          | webhook-handler     | security-auditor          |
| App proxy endpoint        | api-builder         | storefront-builder        |

## Process

### Step 1: Design the API Contract
- Define the HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
- Define the route path following Remix conventions
- Design the request body / query parameters schema
- Design the response shape with proper status codes
- Document error response format

### Step 2: Choose the Route Type
- **Admin route** (`app/routes/app.*.tsx`): Protected by Shopify admin auth
- **API route** (`app/routes/api.*.tsx`): For programmatic access
- **Public route** (`app/routes/public.*.tsx`): For storefront widget calls
- **Webhook route** (`app/routes/webhooks.*.tsx`): For Shopify webhook handlers

### Step 3: Implement the Endpoint

For admin routes:
- Use `authenticate.admin(request)` in loader/action
- Access shop via session: `const { admin, session } = await authenticate.admin(request)`
- Return JSON with proper typing

For public/storefront routes:
- Add CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin with allowlist)
- Validate the request origin or use app proxy authentication
- Rate limit considerations for public endpoints
- Never expose sensitive shop data

For webhook routes:
- Verify HMAC signature via `authenticate.webhook(request)`
- Process asynchronously if heavy work is needed
- Return 200 immediately to avoid Shopify timeout
- Handle idempotency (webhooks can be sent multiple times)

### Step 4: Add Validation
- Validate all input parameters (type, format, required fields)
- Use Zod or manual validation for request body parsing
- Return 400 with descriptive error messages for invalid input
- Sanitize string inputs before database operations

### Step 5: Implement Business Logic
- Keep route files thin — extract logic to service files if complex
- Use Prisma transactions for multi-step operations
- Always scope database queries by shopId
- Handle edge cases (not found, duplicate, unauthorized)

### Step 6: Add Response Headers
- Set `Content-Type: application/json` for JSON responses
- Add CORS headers for public endpoints
- Add cache headers where appropriate

### Step 7: Test the Endpoint
- Test happy path with valid input
- Test with missing required fields
- Test with invalid data types
- Test unauthorized access (wrong shop, no session)
- Test CORS preflight (OPTIONS request) for public endpoints

    23→### Trigger Types
    24→- **Button Click**: Merchant places a button, click opens quiz
    25→- **Timer Delay**: Auto-open after X seconds on page
    26→- **Exit Intent**: Open when mouse moves toward browser close
    27→- **Scroll Depth**: Open after scrolling X% of page
    28→- **URL Parameter**: Open if specific URL param is present

    32→### Step 1: Design the Widget Feature

    36→- Plan animations and transitions

    40→- Use shadow DOM or scoped CSS to avoid theme conflicts

## Agent Orchestration

| Widget Feature          | Primary Agent         | Support Agents                    |
|-------------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Embed block             | storefront-builder    | responsive-builder                |
| Popup/modal             | popup-builder         | storefront-builder                |
| Slide-in panel          | popup-builder         | responsive-builder                |
| Results display         | storefront-builder    | results-builder                   |
| Trigger configuration   | popup-builder         | storefront-builder                |
| Theme compatibility     | responsive-builder    | storefront-builder                |
| Mobile optimization     | responsive-builder    | popup-builder                     |

## Widget Architecture

### Display Modes
- **Inline Embed**: Renders directly in page content via app block
- **Popup Modal**: Overlay triggered by button, timer, exit intent, or scroll
- **Slide-in Panel**: Slides from side of screen with configurable trigger
- **Full Page**: Takes over entire page (for dedicated quiz pages)

### Trigger Types
- **Button Click**: Merchant places a button, click opens quiz
- **Timer Delay**: Auto-open after X seconds on page
- **Exit Intent**: Open when mouse moves toward browser close
- **Scroll Depth**: Open after scrolling X% of page
- **URL Parameter**: Open if specific URL param is present

## Process

### Step 1: Design the Widget Feature
- Determine the display mode and trigger type
- Sketch the layout for desktop and mobile
- Define the interaction flow (open, navigate questions, submit, show results)
- Plan animations and transitions

### Step 2: Implement the Widget
- Build using vanilla JS/CSS (no framework dependencies in storefront)
- Use shadow DOM or scoped CSS to avoid theme conflicts
- Keep bundle size minimal (< 50KB gzipped)
- Load assets asynchronously to avoid blocking page render

### Step 3: Mobile Responsiveness
- Test at breakpoints: 320px, 375px, 414px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px
- Popup should become full-screen on mobile (< 768px)
- Touch targets must be at least 44x44px
- Ensure no horizontal scrolling on any viewport
- Test with virtual keyboard open (form inputs)

### Step 4: Performance
- Lazy load the widget script (do not block page DOMContentLoaded)
- Lazy load images within the quiz (load on question display)
- Minimize DOM operations during quiz navigation
- Use CSS transforms for animations (GPU accelerated)
- Target: < 100ms interaction response time

### Step 5: CSP Compliance
- No inline script tags — use external script files only
- No inline style attributes if CSP restricts them — use class-based styling
- No eval() or Function() constructors
- Load scripts from the app's registered domain only
- Ensure compatibility with Shopify's Content Security Policy

### Step 6: Theme Compatibility
- Test with Dawn (default Shopify theme)
- Test with at least 2 other popular themes
- Respect the shop's color scheme and typography where possible
- Provide CSS custom properties for merchant customization
- Handle RTL layouts if applicable

### Step 7: Accessibility
- All interactive elements must be keyboard navigable
- Add proper ARIA labels and roles
- Ensure color contrast meets WCAG 2.1 AA
- Support screen readers for question/answer navigation
- Focus management when popup opens/closes

Handle a data migration for QuizSnap: $ARGUMENTS

## Agent Orchestration

| Migration Type           | Primary Agent          | Support Agents                   |
|--------------------------|------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Schema migration         | migration-specialist   | database-architect               |
| Data transformation      | migration-specialist   | database-architect               |
| Backfill missing data    | migration-specialist   | database-architect               |
| Cross-model migration    | database-architect     | migration-specialist             |
| Production migration     | migration-specialist   | deploy-specialist                |

## Process

### Step 1: Plan the Migration
- Read current `prisma/schema.prisma` to understand existing state
- Identify what needs to change and why
- Determine if this is additive (safe) or destructive (risky)
- Classify the migration:
  - **Additive**: New model, new field with default, new index
  - **Rename**: Field rename, model rename
  - **Transform**: Change field type, restructure data
  - **Destructive**: Remove field, remove model, change constraints

### Step 2: Assess Impact
- List all files that query the affected models
- Check for hardcoded field names in loaders, actions, and services
- Estimate the number of rows affected
- Calculate expected migration duration for production data volume
- Identify if migration requires downtime

### Step 3: Create Backup Plan
- For production: ensure database backup exists before migration
- Document the current schema state for rollback reference
- Write rollback migration steps (reverse of forward migration)
- Test rollback in development first

### Step 4: Implement the Migration

**For schema changes**:
- Modify `prisma/schema.prisma`
- Run `npx prisma validate` to check syntax
- Run `npx prisma db push` for development
- For production, use `npx prisma migrate dev --name [description]`
- Run `npx prisma generate` to update the client

**For data transformations**:
- Write a migration script in `prisma/migrations/` or a standalone script
- Process records in batches (100-500 at a time) to avoid memory issues
- Use Prisma transactions for atomic batch updates
- Log progress (processed X of Y records)
- Handle failures gracefully (skip and log, or stop)

**For backfills**:
- Query records missing the target data
- Calculate or derive the correct values
- Update in batches with progress logging
- Verify counts match expected totals

### Step 5: Execute the Migration
- Run in development first and verify results
- Check that all queries still work with the new schema
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` to catch any type mismatches
- Run the application and test affected features manually

### Step 6: Verify
- Count records before and after (should match for non-destructive)
- Spot-check data integrity on sample records
- Run all loaders that query affected models
- Check that the admin UI renders correctly with migrated data
- Verify the storefront widget works with migrated data

### Step 7: Production Execution
- Schedule migration during low-traffic period if possible
- Take database backup immediately before migration
- Run migration with monitoring
- Verify production data after migration
- Keep rollback plan ready for 24 hours

## Caution Rules

- NEVER run destructive migrations without explicit confirmation
- ALWAYS back up production data before migrating
- NEVER modify the Session model (Shopify-managed)
- ALWAYS test migrations in development before production
- NEVER use `--accept-data-loss` in production Prisma commands
- ALWAYS process large data sets in batches
- NEVER drop columns/tables that might still be referenced in code

## Output Format

```

- TypeScript: [PASS/FAIL]
- App functionality: [WORKING/BROKEN]

Optimize performance in QuizSnap: $ARGUMENTS

## Agent Orchestration

| Optimization Area       | Primary Agent          | Support Agents                   |
|-------------------------|------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Database queries        | performance-optimizer  | database-architect               |
| Page load speed         | performance-optimizer  | storefront-builder               |
| Widget performance      | storefront-builder     | responsive-builder               |
| API response time       | api-builder            | performance-optimizer            |
| Caching strategy        | cache-manager          | database-architect               |
| Bundle size             | performance-optimizer  | storefront-builder               |
| Memory usage            | performance-optimizer  | database-architect               |

## Process

### Step 1: Profile the Problem
- Identify the specific area mentioned in $ARGUMENTS
- Measure current performance baseline
- For database: check query execution time and query count per page load
- For pages: check Remix loader execution time
- For widget: check script size and Time to Interactive
- For API: check response time at p50, p95, p99

### Step 2: Identify Bottlenecks

**Database Bottlenecks**:
- N+1 queries (multiple queries for related data)
- Missing indexes on frequently queried columns
- Selecting all fields when only a few are needed
- No pagination on list queries
- Expensive aggregations without caching

**Page Load Bottlenecks**:
- Large loader data payloads (sending too much data to client)
- Sequential data fetching (queries that could be parallel)
- Missing loading states causing layout shift
- Unoptimized images

**Widget Bottlenecks**:
- Script blocking page render
- Large bundle size (images, fonts, unnecessary code)
- Excessive DOM manipulation
- Layout thrashing from style recalculations

**API Bottlenecks**:
- No response caching for stable data
- Synchronous processing of background tasks
- Missing database connection pooling
- Large response payloads without pagination

### Step 3: Apply Optimizations

**Database**:
- Add `select` to Prisma queries to fetch only needed fields
- Use `include` with nested `select` for relations
- Add `@@index` directives in schema.prisma for query patterns
- Implement cursor-based pagination for large datasets
- Cache aggregated analytics data with TTL

**Page Load**:
- Use `defer` in Remix loaders for non-critical data
- Parallelize independent Prisma queries with `Promise.all`
- Implement skeleton loading states
- Lazy load below-the-fold components

**Widget**:
- Load script with `async` or `defer` attribute
- Code-split quiz logic from initialization
- Use `IntersectionObserver` for lazy loading images
- Minimize DOM operations with batch updates
- Use CSS animations instead of JavaScript animations

**API**:
- Add `Cache-Control` headers for cacheable responses
- Move heavy processing to background jobs
- Implement response compression (gzip)
- Add pagination with cursor-based approach

### Step 4: Measure Improvement
- Re-run the same profile as Step 1
- Compare before/after metrics
- Verify no functional regressions
- Document the improvement percentage

### Step 5: Add Monitoring
- Add timing logs for critical paths
- Set up alerts for performance regression thresholds
- Document expected performance characteristics

## Output Format

```

- [Metric]: [value]
- [Metric]: [value]

### Bottlenecks Found
1. [Bottleneck description and impact]
2. [Bottleneck description and impact]

### Optimizations Applied
1. [What was changed] — Expected improvement: [X%]
2. [What was changed] — Expected improvement: [X%]

### Results (After)
- [Metric]: [value] ([improvement %])
- [Metric]: [value] ([improvement %])

### Files Modified
- [path] — [what changed]

### Monitoring
- [What metrics to watch going forward]
```

### Step 1: Welcome Screen
- Display app value proposition
- Show what QuizSnap can do (with visual examples)
- Collect merchant's primary use case:
  - Product recommendations
  - Lead generation

  - Fun engagement quizzes

### Step 2: Store Setup
- Auto-detect shop information from Shopify session
- Confirm business category (for template suggestions)

- Configure email notification preferences

### Step 3: First Quiz Creation
- Offer template selection based on use case and category
- Guide through creating first quiz with inline tips
- Pre-populate with sample questions if template chosen
- Show live preview as merchant builds

### Step 4: Product Connection
- Guide merchant to connect products to quiz results
- Explain the recommendation logic
- Offer automatic product mapping based on collections
- Preview the results page with real products

### Step 5: Widget Placement
- Show display mode options (inline, popup, slide-in)

- One-click publish
- Celebration screen with next steps

### Step 1: Check Onboarding State
- Read Shop model's `onboardingCompleted` field
- Check if any quizzes exist (returning user vs new user)
- Determine which onboarding step to show
- Store progress in Shop model or localStorage

- Mark `onboardingCompleted = true` on Shop model when finished
- Track which steps were completed vs skipped
- Fire analytics event for onboarding completion
- Redirect to main dashboard after completion

| Admin route             | admin-builder     | Existing app routes                |
| API route               | api-builder       | Existing API routes                |
| Webhook route           | webhook-handler   | Existing webhook handlers          |
| Polaris component       | admin-builder     | Existing components                |
| Storefront component    | storefront-builder| Existing widget code               |
| Service file            | api-builder       | Existing server utilities          |
| Prisma model            | database-architect| Existing schema patterns           |

## Process

### Step 1: Identify Scaffold Type
- Parse $ARGUMENTS to determine what to scaffold
- Read CLAUDE.md for naming conventions and file locations
- Find the closest existing example to use as a pattern

### Step 2: Generate the Boilerplate

Select the appropriate template based on type:

**Admin Route** (`app/routes/app.[name].tsx`):
- Remix loader with `authenticate.admin(request)`
- Remix action for form submissions
- Polaris Page layout with proper title
- TypeScript types for loader/action data
- Export default component with `useLoaderData` and `useActionData`
- Error boundary export

**API Route** (`app/routes/api.[name].tsx`):
- Loader or action with proper auth method
- Request validation
- JSON response with correct Content-Type
- Error handling with status codes
- CORS headers if public endpoint

**Webhook Route** (`app/routes/webhooks.[topic].tsx`):
- Action function with `authenticate.webhook(request)`
- HMAC validation via Shopify authenticate
- Webhook payload parsing
- Async processing pattern
- 200 OK immediate response

**Polaris Component** (`app/components/[Name].tsx`):
- TypeScript interface for props
- Functional component with Polaris imports
- Loading state variant
- Error state variant
- Empty state variant

**Service File** (`app/services/[name].server.ts`):
- TypeScript interfaces for input/output
- Main function with proper error handling
- Prisma client usage with shop scoping
- Export named functions

**Prisma Model Addition**:
- Model with id, timestamps, and shop relation
- Proper field types and constraints
- Index definitions for query patterns
- Relation to existing models

### Step 3: Apply Project Conventions
- Match import style from existing files (relative vs alias)
- Match export style (default vs named)
- Match naming convention (camelCase functions, PascalCase components)
- Match Polaris component usage patterns from existing routes
- Include proper TypeScript typing (no `any` types)

### Step 4: Wire Up
- Add to navigation if it is a new admin page
- Register webhook in shopify.server.ts if it is a new webhook
- Update Prisma schema and generate client if new model
- Add route to any existing route manifests or menus

### Step 5: Verify
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` to ensure the scaffold compiles
- Verify the file location follows project structure
- Confirm imports resolve correctly

## Scaffold Templates Quick Reference

### Admin Route Skeleton
```
loader: authenticate.admin -> prisma query -> return json
action: authenticate.admin -> validate input -> prisma mutation -> return json
Component: useLoaderData -> Polaris Page + Layout + Cards
```

### API Route Skeleton
```
loader/action: authenticate -> validate -> business logic -> json response
CORS headers for public routes
```

### Webhook Skeleton
```
action: authenticate.webhook -> parse payload -> process -> return 200
```

- [ ] Connect to [related feature]
- [ ] Write tests for [critical paths]

### Verification
- TypeScript: [PASS/FAIL]
- Imports resolve: [YES/NO]
- Follows conventions: [YES/NO]
```

Each template includes:

## Process

### Step 1: Choose Category
- Parse $ARGUMENTS to identify the template category
- Research common quiz patterns for that category
- Define the customer journey (what problem does this quiz solve?)
- Identify 3-5 distinct outcome profiles

### Step 2: Design Questions
- Write 5-10 questions that progressively narrow down recommendations
- Start with broad preference questions, end with specific needs
- Mix question types for engagement:
  - Image choice for visual preferences (e.g., skin type, style)
  - Multiple choice for lifestyle/habits
  - Slider for intensity/budget preferences
  - Rating for priority ranking
- Keep questions concise and conversational in tone
- Ensure every question contributes to the scoring logic

### Step 3: Define Result Profiles
- Create 3-5 distinct outcome profiles
- Each profile needs:
  - Title (e.g., "The Minimalist", "Dry Skin Care Routine")
  - Description (2-3 sentences explaining the recommendation)
  - Image placeholder
  - Product slots (where merchant assigns their products)

### Step 4: Build Score Mappings
- Assign score values to each question option per result profile
- Ensure scoring produces clear differentiation between results
- Test scoring with sample answer combinations:
  - All answers pointing to Profile A should yield Profile A
  - Mixed answers should yield a reasonable result
  - No edge cases produce ties without tiebreaker logic

### Step 5: Create Template Data
- Build the template as a JSON structure that can be imported
- Include all questions, options, result profiles, and score mappings
- Add placeholder text for merchant customization
- Set sensible default widget settings

- Add difficulty level (simple, intermediate, advanced)

    12→
    13→## A/B Test Architecture
    14→
    15→### What Can Be Tested
    16→- Quiz title and description
    17→- Question order and wording
    18→- Question types (e.g., image choice vs text choice)
    19→- Number of questions (short quiz vs long quiz)
    20→- Result page layout and copy
    21→- Widget display mode (popup vs inline vs slide-in)
    22→- Popup trigger timing
    23→- Call-to-action button text and color
    24→- Product recommendation count
    25→
    26→### Traffic Split Model
    27→- Uses the ABTest model: variantA (original), variantB (variation)
    28→- Split percentage configurable (default: 50/50)
    29→- Assignment is sticky per visitor (cookie-based)
    30→- Cookie name: `qs_ab_{testId}`
    31→- Cookie lifetime: 30 days
    32→
    33→## Process
    34→
    35→### Step 1: Define the Test
    36→- Parse $ARGUMENTS for what element to test
    37→- Identify the hypothesis (what change should improve what metric)
    38→- Define the primary metric (completion rate, conversion rate, etc.)
    39→- Define secondary metrics (engagement, time on quiz, etc.)
    40→- Calculate minimum sample size for statistical significance
    41→
    42→### Step 2: Configure Variants
    43→- Create the ABTest record in the database
    44→- Set up variant A (control — current version)
    45→- Set up variant B (treatment — the change)
    46→- Configure the traffic split percentage
    47→- Set the test status to "draft"
    48→
    49→### Step 3: Implement Traffic Splitting
    50→- On widget load, check for existing AB test cookie
    51→- If no cookie, assign variant based on split percentage
    52→- Set cookie with variant assignment
    53→- Load the correct quiz variant based on assignment

Set up an A/B test for QuizSnap: $ARGUMENTS

## Agent Orchestration

| A/B Test Feature        | Primary Agent     | Support Agents                      |
|-------------------------|-------------------|-------------------------------------|
| Test configuration      | ab-testing        | quiz-builder                        |
| Traffic splitting       | ab-testing        | storefront-builder                  |
| Metric tracking         | ab-testing        | analytics-builder                   |
| Statistical analysis    | ab-testing        | analytics-aggregator                |
| Winner declaration      | ab-testing        | quiz-builder                        |

## A/B Test Architecture

### What Can Be Tested
- Quiz title and description
- Question order and wording
- Question types (e.g., image choice vs text choice)
- Number of questions (short quiz vs long quiz)
- Result page layout and copy
- Widget display mode (popup vs inline vs slide-in)
- Popup trigger timing
- Call-to-action button text and color
- Product recommendation count

### Traffic Split Model
- Uses the ABTest model: variantA (original), variantB (variation)
- Split percentage configurable (default: 50/50)
- Assignment is sticky per visitor (cookie-based)
- Cookie name: `qs_ab_{testId}`
- Cookie lifetime: 30 days

## Process

### Step 1: Define the Test
- Parse $ARGUMENTS for what element to test
- Identify the hypothesis (what change should improve what metric)
- Define the primary metric (completion rate, conversion rate, etc.)
- Define secondary metrics (engagement, time on quiz, etc.)
- Calculate minimum sample size for statistical significance

### Step 2: Configure Variants
- Create the ABTest record in the database
- Set up variant A (control — current version)
- Set up variant B (treatment — the change)
- Configure the traffic split percentage
- Set the test status to "draft"

### Step 3: Implement Traffic Splitting
- On widget load, check for existing AB test cookie
- If no cookie, assign variant based on split percentage
- Set cookie with variant assignment
- Load the correct quiz variant based on assignment
- Ensure consistent experience across page loads

### Step 4: Implement Metric Tracking
- Tag all analytics events with the variant identifier
- Track per-variant:
  - Quiz views (impressions)
  - Quiz starts
  - Quiz completions
  - Product clicks
  - Add to cart events
  - Completion rate (completions / starts)
  - Conversion rate (add_to_cart / completions)
- Store variant info in AnalyticsEvent metadata

### Step 5: Build Test Dashboard
- Show test status (draft, running, completed)
- Display per-variant metrics side by side
- Show statistical significance indicator
- Show confidence level (aim for 95%)
- Display estimated time to reach significance
- Add controls: start test, pause test, declare winner

### Step 6: Monitor and Analyze
- Check results daily (or on-demand)
- Calculate statistical significance using chi-squared test
- Flag if one variant is significantly underperforming (safety check)
- Auto-pause if variant B conversion drops below threshold

### Step 7: Declare Winner
- When statistical significance (95% confidence) is reached:
  - Highlight the winning variant
  - Show improvement percentage
  - Offer one-click "apply winner" to make it permanent
- If no significant difference after sufficient sample:
  - Recommend ending the test
  - Suggest a different element to test

## Statistical Method
- Test type: Two-proportion z-test
- Minimum confidence level: 95% (p < 0.05)
- Minimum sample size per variant: 100 conversions
- Recommended runtime: at least 7 days (captures weekly patterns)

## Output Format

```
## A/B Test Report: [Test Name]

### Hypothesis
- [What change is being tested and expected outcome]

### Configuration
- **Variant A (Control)**: [description]
- **Variant B (Treatment)**: [description]
- **Split**: [percentage]
- **Primary Metric**: [metric name]
- **Status**: [draft/running/completed]

### Results (if running/completed)
| Metric            | Variant A | Variant B | Difference |
|-------------------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Impressions       | [count]   | [count]   |            |
| Completions       | [count]   | [count]   |            |
| Completion Rate   | [%]       | [%]       | [+/- %]    |
| Conversions       | [count]   | [count]   |            |
| Conversion Rate   | [%]       | [%]       | [+/- %]    |

### Statistical Significance
- Confidence: [%]
- Significant: [YES/NO]
- Winner: [A/B/None yet]

### Files
- [path] — [purpose]
```

### Step 1: Determine Operation
- Parse $ARGUMENTS: is this an export or import?
- Identify the data type to export/import
- Determine the format (CSV, JSON)
- Check plan gating (export may be a paid feature)

### Step 2: Export Process

**For CSV exports**:
- Query the database with proper shop scoping
- Apply any filters (date range, quiz ID, status)
- Flatten nested data for CSV compatibility (JSON answers become columns)
- Generate CSV with headers as first row
- Stream large exports to avoid memory issues (use chunked processing)
- Return file as downloadable response with proper headers:
  Content-Type: text/csv
  Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="quizsnap-responses-YYYY-MM-DD.csv"

**For JSON exports**:
- Query the database with all related records
- Build the complete object graph (quiz + questions + options + logic + results)
- Strip internal IDs and shop-specific data for portability
- Pretty-print the JSON for readability
- Return as downloadable JSON file

### Step 3: Import Process

**For CSV imports**:
- Parse the uploaded CSV file
- Validate headers match expected format
- Validate each row's data (types, required fields, references)
- Show preview of first 5 rows for confirmation
- Process in batches (100 rows at a time)
- Report success/failure counts

**For JSON imports** (quiz templates):
- Parse the uploaded JSON
- Validate structure matches expected schema
- Check for conflicts (duplicate slugs, etc.)
- Create all records in a transaction (quiz, questions, options, rules, profiles)
- Assign new IDs and link to current shop
- Report what was created

### Step 4: Validate
- Verify exported file opens correctly in target application (Excel for CSV)
- Verify imported data appears correctly in the admin UI
- Check record counts match expectations
- Verify no data corruption (special characters, unicode, line breaks)

### Step 5: Handle Edge Cases
- Empty dataset: return file with headers only (CSV) or empty array (JSON)
- Large dataset (10,000+ rows): stream and paginate
- Special characters in data: proper CSV escaping (quote wrapping)
- Unicode content: UTF-8 BOM for Excel compatibility
- Import conflicts: skip duplicates and report, or offer overwrite option

## Security Rules
- NEVER export data from other shops (always scope by shopId)
- Sanitize imported data before database insertion
- Validate file size limits (max 10MB for imports)
- Validate file type (reject unexpected MIME types)
- Log all export and import operations for audit trail

## Pre-Flight (Read First)
1. Read `CLAUDE.md` fully — 15 Architecture Laws + canonical schema
2. Check CLAUDE.md Section 13 feature status tracker

## Agent Routing

| Review Phase            | Agent              | Focus Area                                  |
|-------------------------|--------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| Automated checks        | `reviewer`         | TypeScript, ESLint, Prisma validate         |
| Security audit          | `security-auditor` | Auth, CSRF, data exposure, shop scoping     |
| Polaris v13 compliance  | `polaris-design-system` | Component props, deprecated patterns   |
| Performance             | `performance-optimizer` | N+1 queries, indexes, bundle size      |
| UX completeness         | `admin-builder`    | Empty states, skeletons, toasts             |

## Phase 1: Automated Checks

```bash
npm run typecheck     # Must show: "Found 0 errors."
npx prisma validate   # Must show: "The schema at ... is valid"
npm run lint          # Zero errors (warnings OK with justification)
```

**Reject immediately if:**
- `npm run typecheck` has ANY errors
- Any `as any`, `: any`, `<any>` types present
- Any `@ts-ignore` without justification
- Prisma schema invalid

## Phase 2: Security Audit

```
AUTH CHECKS:
[ ] Every admin route calls authenticate.admin(request) FIRST
[ ] authenticate.admin() result is awaited
[ ] session.shop captured and used in every WHERE clause
[ ] findUnique results verified against session.shop

SHOP SCOPING:
[ ] db.quiz.findMany({ where: { shop } }) — NOT without shop
[ ] All Prisma queries include shop: session.shop
[ ] update/delete operations include shop in where clause
[ ] NEVER trust shop from request body — always use session.shop

PUBLIC API (api.*.tsx):
[ ] CORS headers on ALL responses including errors
[ ] OPTIONS preflight returns 204
[ ] shop param validated: /^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9\-]*\.myshopify\.com$/
[ ] No authenticate.admin() on public routes

INPUT VALIDATION:
[ ] Zod schema validates all public API inputs
[ ] No $queryRaw with string interpolation
[ ] String lengths bounded
```

## Phase 3: Polaris v13 Compliance

```tsx
// VIOLATIONS to catch:
<Badge status="success">        // WRONG → tone="success"
<Banner status="warning">       // WRONG → tone="warning"
<Button destructive>            // WRONG → tone="critical"
<Button primary>                // WRONG → variant="primary"
<Button plain>                  // WRONG → variant="plain"
<Stack>                         // WRONG → BlockStack or InlineStack
<TextStyle variation="subdued"> // WRONG → <Text tone="subdued">
<Frame><Toast /></Frame>        // WRONG → shopify.toast.show()
import { useFetcher } from "@remix-run/react" // WRONG → "react-router"

// REQUIRED patterns:
shopify.toast.show("msg", { duration: 3000 })  // App Bridge v4 toast
shopify.toast.show("err", { isError: true })   // App Bridge v4 error toast
useIndexResourceState()          // Required for IndexTable selection
```

## Phase 4: Performance Review

```typescript
// RED FLAGS — N+1 queries:
for (const quiz of quizzes) {
  const count = await db.question.count({ where: { quizId: quiz.id } }); // N+1!
}

// CORRECT — use _count:
const quizzes = await db.quiz.findMany({
  include: { _count: { select: { questions: true } } }, // Single query ✓
});

// Missing select on large tables = slow:
await db.quiz.findMany({ where: { shop } }); // Returns ALL fields

// CORRECT — select only needed:
await db.quiz.findMany({
  where: { shop },
  select: { id: true, title: true, status: true, completions: true },
});
```

**Missing Index Check:**
```
Verify in schema.prisma:
- Quiz: @@index([shop, status]) — for filtered list queries
- AnalyticsEvent: @@index([shop, quizId, eventType]) — for funnel
- QuizResponse: @@index([quizId, shop]) — for response queries
- ProductMapping: @@index([shop, status]) — active products
```

## Phase 5: UX Completeness

```
Every page must have:
[ ] LOADING: navigation.state !== "idle" → skeleton or spinner
[ ] EMPTY STATE: EmptyState component when list is empty
[ ] ERROR STATE: Error toast for failed actions
[ ] TOAST: shopify.toast.show() for every mutation (success + error)
[ ] CONFIRMATION: Polaris Modal for destructive actions (or Banner inline)
[ ] DISABLED: Primary action disabled while navigation.state !== "idle"
```

## Critical Schema Field Names

```
WRONG → CORRECT
shopId → shop
shopifyProductId → productGid
isAvailable → status ("active" | "archived")
lastSyncedAt → syncedAt
QuestionOption → Answer (model name)
ResultProfile → ResultPage (model name)
LogicRule → logic JSON field on Question
BillingPlan → Subscription (model name)
```

## Output Format

```
## Code Review: [Description]

### VERDICT: [APPROVED ✅ | NEEDS FIXES ❌ | CONDITIONALLY APPROVED ⚠️]

### Phase 1 — Automated
- TypeScript: PASS (0 errors) | FAIL ([N] errors)
- Prisma: PASS | FAIL
- ESLint: PASS | WARNINGS ONLY

### Phase 2 — Security: [PASS | CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUM]
- Auth: [PASS | FAIL: description + file:line]
- Shop scoping: [PASS | FAIL]
- Public API: [PASS | FAIL | N/A]

### Phase 3 — Polaris v13: [PASS | VIOLATIONS]
- [violation]: [file:line] → change X to Y

### Phase 4 — Performance: [PASS | ISSUES]
- [issue]: description + fix

### Phase 5 — UX: [PASS | INCOMPLETE]
- [missing]: what to add + where

### Mandatory Fixes (block merge):
1. [CRITICAL issue]
   File: [path:line]
   Fix: [exact code]

### Next Action:
[What to do after fixes]
```

[ ] Zod schema validates all public API inputs

```

## Phase 3: Polaris v13 Compliance

```tsx

<Badge status="success">        // WRONG → tone="success"
<Banner status="warning">       // WRONG → tone="warning"
<Button destructive>            // WRONG → tone="critical"
<Button primary>                // WRONG → variant="primary"
<Button plain>                  // WRONG → variant="plain"
<Stack>                         // WRONG → BlockStack or InlineStack
<TextStyle variation="subdued"> // WRONG → <Text tone="subdued">
<Frame><Toast /></Frame>        // WRONG → shopify.toast.show()
import { useFetcher } from "@remix-run/react" // WRONG → "react-router"

// REQUIRED patterns:
shopify.toast.show("msg", { duration: 3000 })  // App Bridge v4 toast
shopify.toast.show("err", { isError: true })   // App Bridge v4 error toast
useIndexResourceState()          // Required for IndexTable selection
```

## Phase 4: Performance Review

```typescript
// RED FLAGS — N+1 queries:
for (const quiz of quizzes) {
  const count = await db.question.count({ where: { quizId: quiz.id } }); // N+1!
}

// CORRECT — use _count:
const quizzes = await db.quiz.findMany({
  include: { _count: { select: { questions: true } } }, // Single query ✓
});

// Missing select on large tables = slow:
await db.quiz.findMany({ where: { shop } }); // Returns ALL fields

// CORRECT — select only needed:
await db.quiz.findMany({
  where: { shop },
  select: { id: true, title: true, status: true, completions: true },
});
```

- AnalyticsEvent: @@index([shop, quizId, eventType]) — for funnel
- QuizResponse: @@index([quizId, shop]) — for response queries
- ProductMapping: @@index([shop, status]) — active products
```

## Phase 5: UX Completeness

```
Every page must have:
[ ] LOADING: navigation.state !== "idle" → skeleton or spinner
[ ] EMPTY STATE: EmptyState component when list is empty
[ ] ERROR STATE: Error toast for failed actions
[ ] TOAST: shopify.toast.show() for every mutation (success + error)
[ ] CONFIRMATION: Polaris Modal for destructive actions (or Banner inline)
[ ] DISABLED: Primary action disabled while navigation.state !== "idle"
```

## Critical Schema Field Names

```
WRONG → CORRECT
shopId → shop
shopifyProductId → productGid
isAvailable → status ("active" | "archived")
lastSyncedAt → syncedAt

npm run build    # Must complete without errors

```bash
shopify app deploy    # Deploys app config + theme extensions

## Pre-Flight (Read First)
1. Read `CLAUDE.md` Section 4 — CANONICAL schema (single source of truth)
2. Read current `prisma/schema.prisma` to understand existing state
3. NEVER modify the Session model

## Agent Routing

| Task Type            | Primary Agent         | Support Agents             |
|----------------------|-----------------------|----------------------------|
| Schema changes       | `prisma-schema`       | `prisma-queries`           |
| Query optimization   | `prisma-queries`      | `performance-optimizer`    |
| Migrations           | `prisma-schema`       | (migration commands below) |
| Seed data            | `prisma-schema`       | `template-builder`         |
| N+1 detection        | `prisma-queries`      | `performance-optimizer`    |

## Canonical Models Reference (CLAUDE.md Section 4)

| Model              | Key Fields                                                      | Constraints                    |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| Session            | id, shop, state, accessToken, scope                             | DO NOT MODIFY — Shopify-managed|
| Quiz               | id, **shop**, title, slug, status, type, settings (JSON)        | @@unique([shop, slug])         |
| Question           | id, quizId, type, title, position, settings (JSON), logic (JSON)| @@index([quizId, position])    |
| Answer             | id, questionId, text, position, score, productTags (JSON)       | @@index([questionId, position])|
| ResultPage         | id, quizId, title, type, minScore, maxScore, matchTags (JSON)   | @@index([quizId, position])    |
| QuizResponse       | id, quizId, **shop**, sessionId, email, answers (JSON), score   | @@index([quizId, shop])        |
| ProductMapping     | id, **shop**, **productGid**, title, tags (JSON), status        | @@unique([shop, productGid])   |
| QuizTemplate       | id, name, category, templateData (JSON), isGlobal, shop?        | @@index([category])            |
| WidgetConfig       | id, **shop** (unique), position, triggerType, styling (JSON)    | @unique on shop                |
| EmailIntegration   | id, **shop**, provider, apiKey, listId                          | @@unique([shop, provider])     |
| ABTest             | id, quizId, **shop**, name, status, variants (JSON)             | @@index([shop, status])        |
| Subscription       | id, **shop** (unique), planId, status, trialEndsAt              | @unique on shop                |
| AnalyticsEvent     | id, **shop**, quizId, eventType, sessionId, data (JSON)         | @@index([shop, quizId, eventType]) |

## CRITICAL: Wrong → Correct Field Names

```
WRONG → CORRECT
shopId → shop
shopifyProductId → productGid
isAvailable → status ("active" | "archived")
lastSyncedAt → syncedAt
QuestionOption → Answer (model name)
ResultProfile → ResultPage (model name)
LogicRule → logic (JSON field on Question — NOT a separate model)
BillingPlan → Subscription (model name)
ScoreMapping → score (Int field on Answer — NOT a separate model)
```

## Process: Schema Changes

```bash
# 1. Edit prisma/schema.prisma matching EXACTLY Section 4 of CLAUDE.md
# 2. Validate syntax
npx prisma validate

# 3. Create named migration (dev)
npx prisma migrate dev --name describe_the_change

# 4. Regenerate client
npx prisma generate

# 5. Run typecheck — fix ALL errors before continuing
npm run typecheck

# PRODUCTION: use migrate deploy (never db push)
npx prisma migrate deploy
```

## Process: Query Optimization

```typescript
// ── WRONG: N+1 pattern ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
for (const quiz of quizzes) {
  const count = await db.question.count({ where: { quizId: quiz.id } }); // N+1!
}

// ── CORRECT: Single query with _count ────────────────────────────────────────
const quizzes = await db.quiz.findMany({
  where: { shop },
  include: { _count: { select: { questions: true } } },
});

// ── WRONG: Over-fetching ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
await db.quiz.findMany({ where: { shop } });  // All fields including settings blob

// ── CORRECT: Select only needed fields ───────────────────────────────────────
await db.quiz.findMany({
  where: { shop },
  select: { id: true, title: true, status: true, completions: true },
});

// ── JSON field: ALWAYS parse with try/catch (Law 6) ──────────────────────────
const settings = (() => {
  try { return JSON.parse(quiz.settings) as Record<string, unknown>; }
  catch { return {}; }
})();

// ── Upsert for idempotent webhook operations ──────────────────────────────────
await db.productMapping.upsert({
  where: { shop_productGid: { shop, productGid } },
  create: { shop, productGid, title, tags: JSON.stringify(tags), syncedAt: new Date() },
  update: { title, tags: JSON.stringify(tags), syncedAt: new Date() },
});

| quiz_abandon        | User leaves without completing   | quizId, lastQuestionId, duration   |
| product_click       | User clicks recommended product  | quizId, productId, resultProfileId |
| add_to_cart         | User adds product from results   | quizId, productId, variantId       |
| email_capture       | User submits email in quiz       | quizId, hasOptIn                   |

## Process

### Step 1: Define Metrics
- Parse $ARGUMENTS to determine which analytics feature to build
- Identify the key metrics (KPIs) this feature should track
- Define how metrics are calculated (counts, rates, averages)
- Determine the time granularity (hourly, daily, weekly, monthly)

### Step 2: Implement Event Tracking
- Add tracking calls in the storefront widget for user actions
- Send events to the public API endpoint (`/api/analytics`)
- Store events in the AnalyticsEvent model with proper metadata
- Ensure events include quizId and shopId for proper scoping
- Batch events if multiple fire in quick succession

### Step 3: Build Aggregation Layer
- Create server-side functions to aggregate raw events into metrics
- Key aggregations:
  - Completion rate: quiz_complete / quiz_start
  - Conversion rate: add_to_cart / quiz_complete
  - Average quiz duration: avg(completedAt - startedAt)
  - Drop-off by question: count(question_answer) grouped by questionId
  - Top products clicked: count(product_click) grouped by productId
- Cache aggregated results for dashboard performance
- Support date range filtering

### Step 4: Build Dashboard UI
- Use Polaris components (Card, DataTable, IndexTable)
- Build summary cards: total responses, completion rate, conversion rate
- Build time-series chart for responses over time
- Build funnel visualization (view > start > complete > convert)
- Build per-question breakdown table
- Add date range picker (7d, 30d, 90d, custom)

### Step 5: Build Reports
- Individual quiz performance report
- Question-level analytics (answer distribution, drop-off)
- Product recommendation effectiveness (clicks, adds to cart)
- Comparison report (quiz A vs quiz B)
- Revenue attribution (orders linked to quiz recommendations)

### Step 6: Validate Data
- Verify event counts match expected behavior
- Check for duplicate events (implement idempotency)
- Verify aggregations produce correct numbers
- Test with zero data (empty states)
- Test with large data sets (pagination, performance)

Build an API endpoint for QuizSnap: $ARGUMENTS

## Agent Orchestration

| API Type                  | Primary Agent       | Support Agents            |
|---------------------------|---------------------|---------------------------|
| Admin API (internal)      | api-builder         | validation-specialist     |
| Public storefront API     | storefront-builder  | api-builder, cors-manager |
| Webhook receiver          | webhook-handler     | security-auditor          |
| App proxy endpoint        | api-builder         | storefront-builder        |

## Process

### Step 1: Design the API Contract
- Define the HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
- Define the route path following Remix conventions
- Design the request body / query parameters schema
- Design the response shape with proper status codes
- Document error response format

### Step 2: Choose the Route Type
- **Admin route** (`app/routes/app.*.tsx`): Protected by Shopify admin auth
- **API route** (`app/routes/api.*.tsx`): For programmatic access
- **Public route** (`app/routes/public.*.tsx`): For storefront widget calls
- **Webhook route** (`app/routes/webhooks.*.tsx`): For Shopify webhook handlers

### Step 3: Implement the Endpoint

For admin routes:
- Use `authenticate.admin(request)` in loader/action
- Access shop via session: `const { admin, session } = await authenticate.admin(request)`
- Return JSON with proper typing

For public/storefront routes:
- Add CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin with allowlist)
- Validate the request origin or use app proxy authentication
- Rate limit considerations for public endpoints
- Never expose sensitive shop data

For webhook routes:
- Verify HMAC signature via `authenticate.webhook(request)`
- Process asynchronously if heavy work is needed
- Return 200 immediately to avoid Shopify timeout
- Handle idempotency (webhooks can be sent multiple times)

### Step 4: Add Validation
- Validate all input parameters (type, format, required fields)
- Use Zod or manual validation for request body parsing
- Return 400 with descriptive error messages for invalid input
- Sanitize string inputs before database operations

### Step 5: Implement Business Logic
- Keep route files thin — extract logic to service files if complex
- Use Prisma transactions for multi-step operations
- Always scope database queries by shopId
- Handle edge cases (not found, duplicate, unauthorized)

### Step 6: Add Response Headers
- Set `Content-Type: application/json` for JSON responses
- Add CORS headers for public endpoints
- Add cache headers where appropriate

### Step 7: Test the Endpoint
- Test happy path with valid input
- Test with missing required fields
- Test with invalid data types
- Test unauthorized access (wrong shop, no session)
- Test CORS preflight (OPTIONS request) for public endpoints

| Page load speed         | performance-optimizer  | storefront-builder               |
| Widget performance      | storefront-builder     | responsive-builder               |
| API response time       | api-builder            | performance-optimizer            |
| Caching strategy        | cache-manager          | database-architect               |

## Process

### Step 1: Profile the Problem
- Identify the specific area mentioned in $ARGUMENTS
- Measure current performance baseline
- For database: check query execution time and query count per page load
- For pages: check Remix loader execution time
- For widget: check script size and Time to Interactive
- For API: check response time at p50, p95, p99

### Step 2: Identify Bottlenecks

**Database Bottlenecks**:
- N+1 queries (multiple queries for related data)
- Missing indexes on frequently queried columns
- Selecting all fields when only a few are needed
- No pagination on list queries
- Expensive aggregations without caching

**Page Load Bottlenecks**:
- Large loader data payloads (sending too much data to client)
- Sequential data fetching (queries that could be parallel)
- Missing loading states causing layout shift
- Unoptimized images

**Widget Bottlenecks**:
- Script blocking page render
- Large bundle size (images, fonts, unnecessary code)
- Excessive DOM manipulation
- Layout thrashing from style recalculations

**API Bottlenecks**:
- No response caching for stable data
- Synchronous processing of background tasks
- Missing database connection pooling
- Large response payloads without pagination

### Step 3: Apply Optimizations

**Database**:
- Add `select` to Prisma queries to fetch only needed fields
- Use `include` with nested `select` for relations
- Add `@@index` directives in schema.prisma for query patterns
- Implement cursor-based pagination for large datasets
- Cache aggregated analytics data with TTL

**Page Load**:
- Use `defer` in Remix loaders for non-critical data
- Parallelize independent Prisma queries with `Promise.all`
- Implement skeleton loading states
- Lazy load below-the-fold components

**Widget**:
- Load script with `async` or `defer` attribute
- Code-split quiz logic from initialization
- Use `IntersectionObserver` for lazy loading images
- Minimize DOM operations with batch updates
- Use CSS animations instead of JavaScript animations

**API**:
- Add `Cache-Control` headers for cacheable responses
- Move heavy processing to background jobs
- Implement response compression (gzip)
- Add pagination with cursor-based approach

- Re-run the same profile as Step 1

- Verify no functional regressions
- Document the improvement percentage

- Add timing logs for critical paths

Test a feature in QuizSnap: $ARGUMENTS

## Agent Orchestration

| Test Type               | Primary Agent     | Support Agents                     |
|-------------------------|-------------------|------------------------------------|
| Unit tests              | test-writer       | —                                  |
| Integration tests       | test-writer       | api-builder                        |
| Component tests         | test-writer       | admin-builder                      |
| E2E flow tests          | test-writer       | storefront-builder                 |
| Load/stress tests       | test-writer       | performance-optimizer              |

## Process

### Step 1: Identify Test Cases
- Parse $ARGUMENTS to determine what feature to test
- Read the feature's implementation files
- Identify the critical paths that must work
- List edge cases and error scenarios
- Categorize tests by type (unit, integration, component)

### Step 2: Plan Test Coverage

**For Loader/Action functions**:
- Valid request with correct session returns expected data
- Missing session returns 401/redirect
- Invalid input returns 400 with error messages
- Database errors are handled gracefully
- Shop scoping prevents cross-shop data access

**For UI Components**:
- Component renders with required props
- Component handles loading state
- Component handles error state
- Component handles empty state
- User interactions trigger correct callbacks

**For API Endpoints**:
- Valid request returns correct response shape
- CORS headers are present on public endpoints
- Rate limiting works (if implemented)
- Webhook HMAC validation works

**For Quiz Logic**:
- Score calculation produces correct results
- Branching logic follows correct path
- Skip logic skips the right questions
- All paths reach a valid result profile

### Step 3: Write Tests
- Create test files in `__tests__/` or alongside source files as `*.test.ts`
- Use Vitest as the test runner (standard for Remix apps)
- Mock Prisma client for database tests
- Mock Shopify session for auth-dependent tests
- Use `@testing-library/react` for component tests

### Step 4: Run Tests
Run `npx vitest run` for all tests, or `npx vitest run [test-file-path]` for specific files.
Use `npx vitest [test-file-path]` for watch mode during development.

### Step 5: Analyze Results
- Check pass/fail count
- Review any failures — determine if test or code is wrong
- Check coverage report if available
- Identify untested critical paths

### Step 6: Report
- Summarize what was tested
- List any failures and their root cause
- Recommend additional test cases if gaps exist

## Test Patterns

### Mocking Prisma
```typescript
const mockPrisma = {
  quiz: { findMany: vi.fn(), create: vi.fn(), update: vi.fn() },
  question: { findMany: vi.fn(), create: vi.fn() },
};
```

### Mocking Shopify Auth
```typescript
const mockSession = { shop: "test-shop.myshopify.com", accessToken: "token" };
vi.mock("~/shopify.server", () => ({
  authenticate: { admin: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ session: mockSession }) },
}));
```

### Testing Loader
```typescript
const response = await loader({ request: new Request(url), params: {}, context: {} });
const data = await response.json();
expect(data.quizzes).toHaveLength(3);
```

## Output Format

```
## Test Report: [Feature Name]

### Coverage
- Tests written: [count]
- Tests passing: [count]
- Tests failing: [count]
- Critical paths covered: [count]/[total]

### Test Cases
| Test Name                    | Type        | Status |
|------------------------------|-------------|--------|
| [test description]           | [unit/int]  | [P/F]  |

### Failures
1. [Test name]: [Failure reason and suggested fix]

### Gaps
- [Untested scenarios that should be covered]

### Files Created
- [path] — [what it tests]
```

Build an onboarding flow for QuizSnap: $ARGUMENTS

## Agent Orchestration

| Onboarding Feature      | Primary Agent        | Support Agents                     |
|-------------------------|----------------------|------------------------------------|
| Setup wizard            | onboarding-builder   | admin-builder                      |
| First quiz guide        | onboarding-builder   | quiz-builder                       |
| Progress tracking       | onboarding-builder   | database-architect                 |
| Contextual help         | onboarding-builder   | admin-builder                      |
| Template selection      | template-builder     | onboarding-builder                 |

## Onboarding Steps

### Step 1: Welcome Screen
- Display app value proposition
- Show what QuizSnap can do (with visual examples)
- Collect merchant's primary use case:
  - Product recommendations
  - Lead generation
  - Customer segmentation
  - Fun engagement quizzes

### Step 2: Store Setup
- Auto-detect shop information from Shopify session
- Confirm business category (for template suggestions)
- Set default quiz styling based on shop theme colors
- Configure email notification preferences

### Step 3: First Quiz Creation
- Offer template selection based on use case and category
- Guide through creating first quiz with inline tips
- Pre-populate with sample questions if template chosen
- Show live preview as merchant builds

### Step 4: Product Connection
- Guide merchant to connect products to quiz results
- Explain the recommendation logic
- Offer automatic product mapping based on collections
- Preview the results page with real products

### Step 5: Widget Placement
- Show display mode options (inline, popup, slide-in)
- Guide through placing the quiz on their store
- Offer recommended placement based on use case
- Show preview of quiz on their actual storefront

### Step 6: Publish
- Final review checklist
- One-click publish
- Celebration screen with next steps

## Process

### Step 1: Check Onboarding State
- Read Shop model's `onboardingCompleted` field
- Check if any quizzes exist (returning user vs new user)
- Determine which onboarding step to show
- Store progress in Shop model or localStorage

### Step 2: Build Wizard UI
- Use Polaris components (Page, Card, ProgressBar, Button)
- Build each step as a separate section within the wizard
- Add navigation (Next, Back, Skip)
- Show progress indicator (Step X of 6)
- Persist progress so merchant can leave and return

### Step 3: Implement Step Logic
- Each step has its own validation before proceeding
- Skip logic: some steps can be skipped, others are required
- Default values for skipped optional steps
- Error handling: show inline errors, do not block progress entirely

### Step 4: Build Contextual Help
- Add tooltips on complex features (using Polaris Tooltip)
- Add info banners explaining concepts
- Link to documentation or help articles where available
- Show first-time hints that dismiss after viewing

### Step 5: Track Completion
- Mark `onboardingCompleted = true` on Shop model when finished
- Track which steps were completed vs skipped
- Fire analytics event for onboarding completion
- Redirect to main dashboard after completion

### Step 6: Handle Return Visitors
- If onboarding was completed, skip to dashboard
- If onboarding was partially completed, resume from last step
- Offer "restart onboarding" option in Settings
- Show a checklist on dashboard for incomplete setup tasks

- Skip allowed: [which steps]

### Files
- [path] — [purpose]

### User Experience
- Time to complete: [estimated minutes]
- Can be skipped: [YES/NO]
- Return handling: [resume/restart/skip]

### Quality
- TypeScript: [PASS/FAIL]
- Mobile responsive: [VERIFIED/NOT TESTED]
- Empty state handling: [PASS/FAIL]
```
